I do want to make sure that the Chamber is clear that when we filed a response it was because new witnesses were added to 65 ter without the consent of the Chamber, which is required under the rules. Individual objections, I think, are the subject now, but just so the Chamber knows, we did respond with an objection then. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At all events, I think that it would be better not to make a decision with respect to the witness list for the accused Zigic as we have already heard that next Monday we are going to be faced with a different list. So let us wait and see. And that is the point that Ms. Somers has been making. Authorisation by the Trial Chamber will be needed to change the list that has been fixed with respect to Rule 95 ter. We will have to show discipline in our work. So if a list has been admitted, and if it is known by the parties, disclosed to both parties, the modification of such a list can only take place with the authorisation of the Trial Chamber. So we are not going to take a decision in that matter now but we are going to wait until Monday. The decisions that we can take here and now are the following: The decisions with respect to the motions, the motions by the defence counsels of Zigic and Kos, with respect to the testimony of Witness R; and the admission into evidence of the testimony of Witness R. And it is upon this subject that the Chamber renders its decision. On the 19th of February, 2001, the Defence of the accused Zigic filed a motion for the issuance of a restraining order with respect to the testimony of Witness R, who testified on the 17th of July, 1996, in the Tadic trial, and that he will testify again before this Trial Chamber. Similarly, the Defence of the accused Mr. Zigic has requested that the transcript of the hearing of Witness R be admitted into evidence. On the same day, the Defence of the accused Kos filed a motion for the admission of -- into evidence of the audience of Witness R. On the 2nd of March, 2001, the Prosecution responded and said that he was not in opposition to the admission of the transcript of the hearing and this was reiterated by them today, and that if the Chamber was to call Witness R, the address of that witness must not be communicated to anybody but the Trial Chamber, only to the Trial Chamber. The Chamber notes that the accusation and the Defence of the accused Kos, as well as the Defence counsel of the accused Zigic, at least as a subsidiary, are in agreement with respect to the admission of the transcript of Witness R into evidence. In light of this agreement, which is not manifestly contrary to an equitable trial or the interests of justice, the Chamber considers that it is not necessary to render any coercive measures with respect to Witness R. Therefore, the Trial Chamber decides to accept the transcript of the testimony of Witness R, with the caveat that it does not -- it will not at this time state what the -- what weight it will give to that evidence. That is the decision. Second, the second decision is with respect to the adoption of the expert witnesses in Mr. Radic's defence, and therefore we are rendering the following decision. On the 31th of January, 2001, the defence of Mr. Radic proposed the admission into evidence of the reports of the following expert witnesses: Madam Ana Najman, Mr. Bernard van den Bussche, Mr. Nenad Kecmanovic, and Mr. Stanko Beatovic. The reports of the psychiatric and psychological experts, of Mr. Bernard van den Bussche and Madam Ana Najman are part of the file already, as ordered by the Trial Chamber, and therefore they will have the reference numbers accorded them by the Registry. The parties can simply formulate their observations and the Chamber will then attach weight to them. After the observations made by the Prosecution with respect to Ms. Najman's report, the Trial Chamber has authorised the cross-examination of this, so that on the 6th of March, 2001, the Prosecution did have the possibility of expressing its viewpoint, that is to say its reasons, stipulating its reasons. The Chamber also notes that the observations made by the Prosecution with respect to the report of Mr. van den Bussche, according to which the report was not compiled in conformity with the norms of his profession, the Chamber decides that the Prosecution will have at its disposal 20 minutes for cross-examination of this same expert witness with respect to those points, in other words, the report -- in other words, in conformity with the norms of the profession. The report of Mr. Beatovic with respect to legislation on rape in the ex-Yugoslavia, the Chamber notes that this report has to do with the question of applicable law in ex-Yugoslavia in the matter of rape in view of the fact that the accused Radic has been charged with that crime. The Defence of the accused Radic -- the Defence has stated that the report by Mr. Beatovic is not relevant and, yesterday, during the proceedings, Ms. Somers announced that the two parties would be meeting to discuss the report once again. Ms. Somers has just told us -- has just briefed us of the situation and brought us up to date. Therefore, faced with a situation of this kind, the Trial Chamber cannot deny all probative value to this report and adopts into evidence it without speaking of the weight that it will ascribe to that document. The accusation will have at its disposal 20 minutes to present its own views with respect to this report. The decision on the motion -- on the report by Mr. Kecmanovic with respect to an analysis of the armed conflict in Yugoslavia, the Chamber notes that this report deals with the political and historical aspects of the conflict in ex-Yugoslavia. The Prosecution objected to the adoption of the report by Mr. Kecmanovic because, in their opinion, the report is irrelevant. The accusation -- the Prosecution wishes to hold a cross-examination of that expert witness, if the report adopts -- if the Chamber adopts the report, and has also said that it intends to make a written response. The Defence has therefore decided not to call Mr. Kecmanovic to testify. The Chamber adopts the report of Mr. Kecmanovic, together with the written response from the Prosecution, without attaching weight to the evidence in -- at this stage of the trial. Those are the oral decisions which the Chamber has made, and we should also like to tell you that next week there will be three written decisions, three written rulings. That is as much as I can tell you at this point in time. Ms. Susan Somers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I ask just for a clarification. On the 20 minutes as to van den Bussche and Beatovic, is that 20 minutes of live cross-examination the Chamber is giving us? I wasn't clear when it said "observations." Is it live cross-examination we will be able to have then?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I see Mr. Deretic on his feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry. Just a second, Mr. Deretic. I'm going to give the floor to Mr. Fila.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I understood correctly, next week both experts are to appear before the Trial Chamber, Beatovic and van den Bussche. All right. Because I don't know this latter gentleman, the registry will inform me when he's able to appear and I will make my own arrangements. And as far as Mr. Beatovic is concerned, I will contact him myself and we'll bring him in somehow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm going to ask for the good offices of the registry to assist us in this matter, and I count on their cooperation. Isn't that so, Madam Registar?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, then. We can count on the registry, then. You have the floor, Mr. Deretic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I have two more questions to raise and I would appreciate your assistance and opinion on them. The first one relates to the date. In fact, I would like to ask whether there are any changes in the schedule of presentation of Prosecution witnesses concerning the accused Zigic. Is it the 26th of March and is it still true that we will have three weeks running?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can already answer. We have not made any changes in the schedule. We still have a very tight schedule and we are trying to keep to it as much as we can. So we will stand by the dates that we have determined and which have been notified to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My other question is the following: My colleague Mitrovic is our legal advisor on our team, and we would like to ask the Chamber's permission that Ms. Ljiljana Mitrovic be allowed to question the witnesses presented by the Defence. And we have already addressed this question to the accused, who is in agreement, and we have also addressed this question to the registry, which informed us that we should ask the Trial Chamber. In case the Trial Chamber agrees, the status of my colleague, Ms. Mitrovic would not change; she would remain on the team as in the capacity of a legal advisor. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Deretic, I would only like to make one observation. Your request would have been more appropriate yesterday, but we are going to consider it anyway. I'm not sure if you understand why I'm saying this. Because we are treating parties equitably here and we have already treated the same case with respect to Jelena Nikolic. So yesterday would have been a more appropriate time to address this, but thank you very much for this suggestion. I think we have no more issues to address now, which means that we shall resume our work on Monday, 9.20, and we have finished for today. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
